problem: Existing VLN and VLN-CE benchmarks and simulators are essentially static and lack moving obstacles such as humans, so agents are never tested on predicting and avoiding dynamic obstacles or on physically realistic collisions.
motivation: Real home robots share space with moving people, so agents must follow instructions while avoiding collisions with humans. The paper builds a physics-based, hardware-agnostic testbed and uses a zero-shot GPT-4o-mini agent to show the new difficulties this task brings.
key_idea: Extend VLN-CE to AdaVLN by adding animated moving humans in Matterport3D scenes, using an IsaacSim-based AdaSimulator with a freeze-time mechanism and a small AdaR2R sample dataset.
insight: Zero-shot GPT-4o-mini agents have very high collision rates (average combined NC 0.64, mostly environmental) because they hallucinate clear paths and fail to recognise the humans as obstacles. Full physics also makes wall collisions unrecoverable, because the Jetbot flips or gets stuck with no reverse action, unlike Habitat's wall sliding. No ablations are run.
method: AdaVLN task: VLN-CE in Matterport3D with continuous actions (turn ±15°, forward 0.25 m, stop), 115° egocentric RGB-D view, a 50-step limit, and moving humans that must be avoided.
Freeze-time: the simulation pauses while the agent computes its action, making results independent of hardware and inference speed. It is toggleable.

AdaSimulator: an IsaacSim extension that sets up collider meshes, a differential-drive NVIDIA Jetbot (wheel radius 0.035 m, wheel base 0.1 m), camera render products, lighting and animated humans (customised omni.anim.people). It has GUI and headless modes and a ROS2 interface.

AdaR2R (Sample): 9 episodes across 3 HM3Dv2 example scenes, with 1-2 manually placed humans per episode patrolling NavMesh waypoint loops that interfere with the reference path. Mean geodesic distance is 5.84 m.
Baseline GPT agent: zero-shot GPT-4o-mini on 640x360 RGB. Each step it produces semantic observations, a long-term plan, a reflection on previous steps and then an action, within 200 output tokens.
Metrics: Navigation Collisions (NC), the fraction of navigation time spent in collision, reported as environmental NC, human NC and combined NC.

setting.observation: egocentric 115-degree front-facing RGB-D rendered; the agent uses only RGB down-scaled to 640x360
setting.action_space: low-level: turn left/right 15° at 30°/s, forward 0.25 m at 0.5 m/s, stop (each action takes 2 s)

numbers.extra: 50-step limit, freeze-time, RGB only, 1-2 humans per episode
numbers.evidence: Table 1 Normalized Collision values across episodes, Average row: 0.63 / 0.01 / 0.64

numbers_note: No SR, SPL or NE reported; only collision metrics on 9 sample episodes. The 'val' split label is a placeholder for a sample dataset with no official split.
results: The zero-shot GPT-4o-mini baseline has an average combined NC of 0.64 (environmental 0.63, human 0.01) over the 9 episodes. Collisions are dominated by walls: the robot gets stuck and makes little effort to avoid humans. There is no stronger baseline; this is a demonstration of the task.
limitations: The dataset is tiny (9 episodes, 3 scenes, manually placed humans) and only one weak zero-shot baseline is evaluated.
No standard navigation metrics (SR, SPL) are reported and there is no comparison with other agents or with HA3D.
The physics setup (Jetbot flipping, no reverse action) and unrealistic human models may confound the evaluation of navigation ability.
